Question: Let \(\Gamma\) be a non-uniform arithmetic lattice in \(\mathrm{SO}^+(n,1)\), the identity component of the isometry group of hyperbolic \(n\)-space, with \(n\ge 4\). Here non-uniform means that \(\Gamma\) acts discretely with finite covolume but noncompact quotient. A surface subgroup of \(\Gamma\) means a subgroup isomorphic to the fundamental group of a closed surface of genus \(g\ge 2\), and a thin surface subgroup means such a subgroup that has infinite index in \(\Gamma\) and is Zariski dense in \(\mathrm{SO}^+(n,1)\). Which of the following is the strongest existence statement valid in this setting?
Predicted label: 'D'
Predicted text: '\\(\\Gamma\\) contains a thin surface subgroup.'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: '\\(\\Gamma\\) contains a thin surface subgroup.'
Exact Match: 1.0
